short_answer: Will Rogers is a handicapper name sold through WagerTalk, a Las Vegas pick marketplace with written terms and a refund policy. His page was active on 17 Nov 2026, with dated plays for that week and a daily report. The same bio, streaks and prices also appear on a site called StatSalt. In that narrow sense the service is real and selling.

Whether the picks make money over time is a separate question. The page shows streaks such as "48-29 (+64.52)" on football sides rated 4% or higher and "17-4 (+61.35u) RECORD WITH NFL MAX PLAYS!" Each starts and stops where the seller chose. The Last 20 table on the same page showed 9 wins and 11 losses when we counted it.

His bio gives no real name, no city and no years, only that he has "rubbed shoulders with the rich and big players" and had "stellar results over the past decade." We found almost no independent buyer posts about him. Treat him as an unproven seller and record every pick yourself.
pricing_intro: All prices below were on the Will Rogers WagerTalk page on 17 Nov 2026. WagerTalk shows a higher list price next to most sale prices; we give both. The All Access passes on the page are WagerTalk passes, and the page does not say they cover only his picks.

guarantee: The guarantee is an extra you pay for. A $5.00 play costs $8.00 with it. WagerTalk says the option "backs your purchase with 100% in credits" and applies "If your daily pick(s) package does not result in an overall profit across all included plays." The paid amount comes back as account credit for a future purchase, not as cash.

The WagerTalk refund policy says "All Sales are Final and products are sold “as is”" and that no refund is issued once a product has been purchased, delivered or viewed. The site terms add that the buyer's exclusive remedy is a refund of the price paid or replacement of the product, at WagerTalk's option. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered.

Each streak starts on a date the seller chose, and units assume a stake the page does not explain. The same page carried a Last 20 table that we counted at 9 wins and 11 losses on 17 Nov 2026. That is a small sample too, but it shows how much a hand picked streak can differ from the most recent plays.

our_data.context: For scale: the streaks on his page run from about 57% to 85% winners, while his Last 20 table showed 45%. customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence on Will Rogers is close to nil. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found almost no independent buyer posts about Will Rogers. On TheRX his name shows up mainly in a list of WagerTalk services members may not post, and in reposted plays with no results attached. The only performance figures come from WagerTalk and a mirror site, StatSalt: hot streaks on one side and a Last 20 table at 9 wins and 11 losses on the other. We found no buyer complaints and no buyer praise. His bio points to the 2025/26 season, so his public history may simply be short.

The WagerTalk page shows a three day leaderboard entry of 6-2 and $1,168 profit next to a Last 20 table that we counted at 9 wins and 11 losses. WagerTalk grades and sells the picks, so neither figure is independent.
TheRX lists Will Rogers, and all WagerTalk handicappers, among the services members may not post in its daily service play threads. We found no post there giving his results.

Our Reddit archive searches for Will Rogers in r/SportsBettingPicks and r/sportsbettingadvice returned only unrelated posts, and the searches of r/sportsbook and r/sportsbetting timed out. Web searches found no SBR, Covers or TheRX thread about his results and no Better Business Bureau, court or regulator record.

conflicts: WagerTalk sells his picks, grades his record, writes his bio and runs the leaderboard that ranks him. None of those numbers is independent of the seller.

TheRX, a large betting forum, lists "All Wagertalk Cappers" and "Will Rogers" among the services members may not post in its daily service play threads. The rule does not say why, and it says nothing about the quality of the picks, but it means paid plays are rarely shared and checked there.
WagerTalk's terms describe the site content as for entertainment and amusement purposes only and make no promise about results.
strengths: Sold through a marketplace with a named Las Vegas seller address, written terms and a refund policy.
Prices are published for every play and pass, and single plays were on sale for $5.
The page shows a Last 20 table with losses as well as wins.
concerns: No full public record. Every headline number is a streak chosen by the seller.
The guarantee costs extra and pays in site credit, never cash. All sales are final.
The bio gives no real name, place or history that a buyer could check.
Almost no independent buyer posts exist, good or bad.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, active seller on WagerTalk, a Las Vegas marketplace with written terms, and his page was updated on 17 Nov 2026. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because no full record of every pick is published, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Will Rogers cost?

On 17 Nov 2026 single plays were $5.00 ($8.00 with the guarantee), short sport passes were $49.00, and a one year pass was $1188.00. WagerTalk all access passes ran from $39.00 for a day to $1,999.00 for a year.
Does Will Rogers have a verified record?
No. The page shows streaks such as 48-29 on football sides rated 4% or higher, all graded by WagerTalk. The Last 20 table on the same page was 9 wins and 11 losses when we counted it.

At $5 a play the price is low, but nothing shows the picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays. The guarantee only returns site credit, and your betting losses are never covered.
